verses.text: The LORD went on speaking to Job:
Will the one who disputes with the Almighty keep arguing? Let the one who challenges God give an answer.
Then Job answered the LORD:
I’m so small. What could I possibly say to you? I put my hand over my mouth.
I’ve spoken once, and I won’t answer again. I’ve spoken twice, and I won’t say any more.
Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind:
Now brace yourself like a man. I’ll ask the questions, and you’ll answer me.
Will you overturn my judgment? Will you condemn me so you can claim you’re in the right?
Is your arm as strong as God’s? Can your voice thunder like his?
Go ahead and clothe yourself with splendor and dignity. Put on honor and majesty.
Pour out the full force of your anger. Look at every proud person and bring them down.
Look at every proud person and humble them. Crush the wicked where they stand.
Bury them together in the dust. Bind their faces in that hidden place.
Then even I will admit that your own right hand can save you.
Look at Behemoth. I made him just as I made you. He eats grass like an ox.
Look at the strength in his thighs and the power in the muscles of his belly.
He swings his tail like a cedar. The tendons of his thighs are tightly woven together.
His bones are like bronze pipes, and his limbs are like bars of iron.
He ranks first among God’s works. The one who made him gives him his sword.
The mountains grow food for him, where all the wild animals play.
He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds in the marsh.
The lotus plants shade him, and the willows along the stream surround him.
When the river floods, he doesn’t flinch. He stays calm even if the Jordan rises to his mouth.
Can anyone catch him while he’s watching or pierce his nose with a snare?
